---
title: "Trigger release notes workflows manually"
subtitle: "ValidMind release notes guides"
---

Manually run the release notes automation for a specific release tag using GitHub Actions.


::: {.callout} 
Manual `workflow_dispatch` is *ungated* — it runs regardless of the defined `RELEASE_AUTOMATION` variable on `validmind/installation` or `validmind/validmind-library`.
:::

## Prerequisites

- Write access (or equivalent) to the `validmind/release-notes` repository so you can use **Run workflow**.
- The release tag you want to document already exists on the source repository.
- Repository secrets and variables configured — refer to the [Access requirements](access-requirements.qmd) for setup.


## When would a human manually trigger release notes workflows?

- [x] When you need to rerun workflows for a particular release. (This will usually refresh any open `release-notes` branch with editing protections in place if any automated branches/PRs exist.)
- [x] When an automatic tag-push dispatch did not run or failed to run. (Edge-case, should be rare.)

## Which workflow should be triggered?

All three listener workflows live in `validmind/release-notes` under **Actions**:

| Workflow | GitHub Actions name | Enter this tag format | Source repo |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Library release notes | **Library release notes** | `v2.13.5` (semver) | [`validmind/validmind-library`](https://github.com/validmind/validmind-library/tags){target="_blank"} |
| Monthly release notes | **Monthly release notes** | `cmvm/26.06.01` (stable monthly ending in `.01`) | `validmind/installation` |
| Patch release notes | **Patch release notes** | `cmvm/26.06.07` (not ending in `.01`)| `validmind/installation` |

::: {.column-margin}
For track-specific behavior after the workflow completes, refer to:

- [Library release automation](library/automation.qmd)
- [Patch release automation](patch/automation.qmd)
- [Monthly release automation](monthly/automation.qmd)

:::

## How does a human manually trigger a release notes workflow?

1. Open: `https://github.com/validmind/release-notes/actions`

2. Select the workflow you want to run from the left sidebar:

   - **Library release notes**
   - **Monthly release notes**
   - **Patch release notes**

3. Click the **Run workflow**:

  - **Use workflow from** — `main` (production). For feature-branch testing, select your branch; checkout uses `ref: ${{ github.ref }}`, so scripts and workflow YAML both come from the selected branch.
  - **{release-type} tag** — Enter in the correct tag format for your release type for the release delta discovery.
  - **Skip LLM `--edit` ...** — Leave this UNCHECKED for library and patch releases, but make sure to CHECK for monthly releases.
  - **Shortcut preflight** (Monthly releases only) — dropdown: `none`, `exists`, or `nonempty` (default `nonempty`)
    - `nonempty` — Shortcut release epic label must exist and have at least one tagged epic or story
    - Use `none` or `exists` only when you understand the Shortcut preflight implications (refer to [monthly release automation](monthly/automation.qmd))
    - Tag-push `repository_dispatch` runs always use `nonempty`; this dropdown applies to manual `workflow_dispatch` only

::: {.callout}
Run **one workflow at a time per tag**. Each track workflow uses a concurrency group keyed on the tag (`library-${{ tag }}`, `patch-${{ tag }}`, `monthly-${{ tag }}`) so duplicate dispatches for the same tag queue rather than overlap. Parallel runs for the *same* version can still race on Shortcut story creation if concurrency is bypassed — avoid double-triggering the same tag.

:::

4. Click **Run workflow**.
